# zenith_tx - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/zenith-tx/0.0.8/zenith_tx/

## Expand description

Transaction engine and audit contract for Zenith.

Owns the v0 transaction op set and the apply/dry-run engine, referential- integrity and ID-uniqueness enforcement, the transaction-result contract (status, diagnostics, source diff, scene diff, affected node IDs, audit preview and audit record), and audit record production. Both the CLI and the future MCP surface sit on top of this crate; neither reimplements it.

# zenith_render - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/zenith-render/0.0.8/zenith_render/

## Expand description

CPU PNG reference renderer for Zenith.

Owns the raster backend adapter trait (tiny-skia is the first engine), deterministic PNG production from a scene display list, SVG and raster image decode, glyph rasterization, and enforcement of all raster-time determinism rules. Backend types never appear in the public API.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [PdfOptions](https://docs.rs/struct.PdfOptions.html)
- Options controlling PDF emission.
- [Raster](https://docs.rs/struct.RasterImage.html)- Image
- A rasterized image in straight-alpha RGBA8 format (row-major).
- [Render](https://docs.rs/struct.RenderError.html)- Error
- An error produced by the rasterization or encoding pipeline.
- [Tiny](https://docs.rs/struct.TinySkiaBackend.html)- Skia - Backend
- CPU rasterization backend backed by the `tiny-skia`library.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Raster](https://docs.rs/trait.RasterBackend.html)- Backend
- Trait that abstracts over different CPU rasterization backends.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [composite_](https://docs.rs/fn.composite_spread.html)- spread
- Composite two rasterized pages SIDE BY SIDE into one image with an optional transparent gutter between them.
- [render_](https://docs.rs/fn.render_image.html)- image
- Rasterize `scene`to a`RasterImage`
- [render_](https://docs.rs/fn.render_pdf.html)- pdf
- Render `scene`to a deterministic vector PDF (a single page).
- [render_](https://docs.rs/fn.render_pdf_multi.html)- pdf_ - multi
- Render `scenes`(one per document page, in order) to a single deterministic multi-page vector PDF, sharing one sequential object-id space.
- [render_](https://docs.rs/fn.render_pdf_multi_with.html)- pdf_ - multi_ - with
- Like `render_pdf_multi``PdfOptions`
- [render_](https://docs.rs/fn.render_pdf_with.html)- pdf_ - with
- Like `render_pdf``PdfOptions`
- [render_](https://docs.rs/fn.render_png.html)- png
- Rasterize `scene`and encode the result as PNG bytes.
- [render_](https://docs.rs/fn.render_spread_png.html)- spread_ - png
- Rasterize two scenes (`left`,`right`), composite them SIDE BY SIDE via`composite_spread`

# zenith_scene - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/zenith-scene/0.0.8/zenith_scene/

## Expand description

Backend-neutral scene IR and scene compilation for Zenith.

Owns the display-list primitives (`FillRect`, `DrawGlyphRun`, `PushClip`,
etc.), scene compilation from a validated AST into a z-ordered display list,
opacity/visibility/clip resolution, and exclusion of non-printing nodes.

This crate is the stable contract boundary that every future backend — GPU, PDF, SVG export — will consume.

[§](https://docs.rs#module-layout)Module layout

- `ir`— scene IR types (- `Scene`,- `SceneCommand`,- `Color`,- `SceneGlyph`).
- `color`— sRGB hex parsing →- `Color`.
- `compile`—- `compile(&Document, &dyn FontProvider) -> CompileResult`.

[§](https://docs.rs#quick-start)Quick start

```
use zenith_scene::{Scene, SceneCommand, Color, Paint};
let mut scene = Scene::new(640.0, 360.0);
scene.commands.push(SceneCommand::FillRect {
    x: 0.0, y: 0.0, w: 640.0, h: 360.0,
    paint: Paint::solid(Color::srgb(248, 250, 252, 255)),
});
let json = scene.to_json().expect("serializes");
assert!(json.contains("zenith-scene-v1"));
```
Compile a parsed document into a scene with
[ compile](https://docs.rs/compile/fn.compile.html).

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

# zenith_layout - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/zenith-layout/0.0.8/zenith_layout/

## Expand description

Text-shaping layer for Zenith.

Shapes a text run into positioned glyphs using `rustybuzz` + `ttf-parser`
(the same proven stack as the sibling `oxipdf` project). All third-party
types are confined to `rustybuzz_engine`; downstream crates see only
Zenith-owned records.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use engine::`- [FallbackResult](https://docs.rs/engine/struct.FallbackResult.html);
- `pub use engine::`- [PositionedGlyph](https://docs.rs/engine/struct.PositionedGlyph.html);
- `pub use engine::`- [ShapeRequest](https://docs.rs/engine/struct.ShapeRequest.html);
- `pub use engine::`- [TextDirection](https://docs.rs/engine/enum.TextDirection.html);
- `pub use engine::`- [TextLayoutEngine](https://docs.rs/engine/trait.TextLayoutEngine.html);
- `pub use engine::`- [ZenithGlyphRun](https://docs.rs/engine/struct.ZenithGlyphRun.html);
- `pub use error::`- [LayoutError](https://docs.rs/error/struct.LayoutError.html);
- `pub use font_meta::`- [FaceMetadata](https://docs.rs/font_meta/struct.FaceMetadata.html);
- `pub use font_meta::`- [face_metadata](https://docs.rs/font_meta/fn.face_metadata.html);
- `pub use rustybuzz_engine::`- [RustybuzzEngine](https://docs.rs/rustybuzz_engine/struct.RustybuzzEngine.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [engine](https://docs.rs/engine/index.html)
- Zenith-owned text-layout types and the `TextLayoutEngine`trait.
- [error](https://docs.rs/error/index.html)
- Error types for zenith-layout.
- [font_](https://docs.rs/font_meta/index.html)- meta
- Font face metadata extraction via `rustybuzz::ttf_parser`.
- [rustybuzz_](https://docs.rs/rustybuzz_engine/index.html)- engine
- `rustybuzz`-backed shaping engine for Zenith.

# git-alias 1.2.4 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/git-alias/1.2.4

git-alias-1.2.4 is not a library.

                # Git-Alias

一个快速的 Git 别名工具，支持两种调用方式。

## 特性

- **双模式调用**: 支持直接调用 (- `gs`) 和 g 前缀调用 (- `g s`)
- **119+ 内置别名**: 覆盖所有常用 git 操作
- **自定义别名**: 通过- `~/.git-alias.toml`添加自定义别名
- **Shell 补全**: 支持 bash、zsh、fish 补全脚本
- **高性能**: Rust 编译，启动时间 < 1ms

## 安装

```
```

## 配置

### 添加到 PATH

将以下内容添加到 `.bashrc` 或 `.zshrc`:

```
```

## 使用方法

### 基本命令

```
```

### 子命令

## 别名列表

运行 `g list` 查看所有别名。

**调用规则**:

- 直接调用（如 `gs`,`gps`,`gba`）：必须以`g`开头
- `g`前缀调用（如- `g s`,- `g ps`,- `g ba`）：别名不能以- `g`开头
- 以 `g`开头的别名不支持`g`前缀调用（如`g gps`报错）

### Add (添加)

| 别名 | 命令 |
| `g a` | git add |
| `ga` | git add |
| `g aa` | git add . |
| `gaa` | git add . |

### Status (状态)

| 别名 | 命令 |
| `g s` | git status |
| `gs` | git status |
| `g ss` | git status -s |
| `gss` | git status -s |
| `g sb` | git status -s -b |
| `gsb` | git status -s -b |

### Commit (提交)

| 别名 | 命令 |
| `g cm` | git commit -m |
| `gcm` | git commit -m |
| `g ca` | git commit --amend |
| `gca` | git commit --amend |
| `g cn` | git commit --no-edit --amend |
| `gcn` | git commit --no-edit --amend |

### Push (推送)

| 别名 | 命令 |
| `g ps` | git push |
| `gps` | git push |
| `g psf` | git push --force-with-lease |
| `gpsf` | git push --force-with-lease |
| `g psu` | git push -u origin HEAD |
| `gpsu` | git push -u origin HEAD |

### Pull (拉取)

| 别名 | 命令 |
| `g p` | git pull |
| `gp` | git pull |
| `g pl` | git pull |
| `gpl` | git pull |
| `g pla` | git pull --all -t |
| `gpla` | git pull --all -t |

### Branch (分支)

| 别名 | 命令 |
| `g b` | git branch |
| `gb` | git branch |
| `g ba` | git branch --all |
| `gba` | git branch --all |
| `g bra` | git branch -avv |
| `gbra` | git branch -avv |
| `g bd` | git branch --delete |
| `gbD` | git branch --delete --force |

### Checkout (检出)

| 别名 | 命令 |
| `g co` | git checkout |
| `gco` | git checkout |

| `gc` | git checkout |

| `gcb` | git checkout -b |

### Log (日志)

| `gl` | git log (自定义格式) |

| `g lgg` | git log --graph --oneline --all |
| `g ls` | git log --no-merges |
| `gls` | git log --no-merges |
| `g lsa` | git log --no-merges --all |
| `glsa` | git log --no-merges --all |
| `g lsm` | git log --all |
| `glsm` | git log --all |

| `glp` | git log --oneline --color -p |

# zenith_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/zenith-core/0.0.8/zenith_core/

## Expand description

Foundation crate for Zenith.

Owns the KDL-v2 parser adapter, semantic AST types, canonical formatter, token types and resolution, validation engine with the full diagnostic set, AST-based migrations, and deterministic font and asset resolution. No other Zenith crate is a dependency.

# zenith_session - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/zenith-session/0.0.8/zenith_session/

## Expand description

zenith-session: local-machine history/session state for `.zen` documents.

Pure crate with injected fs/clock/rng adapters; never depended on by the deterministic render pipeline.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [adapter](https://docs.rs/adapter/index.html)
- Injected adapter traits for filesystem, clock, and RNG access.
- [bundle](https://docs.rs/bundle/index.html)
- Portable, deterministic document-store bundle (`*.zenithbundle`).
- [datadir](https://docs.rs/datadir/index.html)
- Platform data-directory resolution for zenith-session.
- [docid](https://docs.rs/docid/index.html)
- Document-identity minting: 128-bit ULID encoded as 26 Crockford base-32 chars. Deterministic under injected Clock + Rng for testability.
- [error](https://docs.rs/error/index.html)
- `SessionError`
- [gc](https://docs.rs/gc/index.html)
- Object garbage collection.
- [global](https://docs.rs/global/index.html)
- Global cross-document LRU storage cap.
- [identity](https://docs.rs/identity/index.html)
- Document-identity reconciliation: bind a `.zen`’s doc-id to local history, detecting first-edit / move / copy / adoption. Pure over injected adapters.
- [layout](https://docs.rs/layout/index.html)
- Pure path-builder helpers for the zenith store layout.
- [manifest](https://docs.rs/manifest/index.html)
- History records and the append-only JSONL manifest.
- [previews](https://docs.rs/previews/index.html)
- Preview-artifact records: schema and append-only JSONL log.
- [retention](https://docs.rs/retention/index.html)
- Time-Machine-style retention thinning for Tier-2 version history.
- [revspec](https://docs.rs/revspec/index.html)
- Revision-spec resolution: map a revspec string to a session record id.
- [runs](https://docs.rs/runs/index.html)
- Agent-run provenance records: schema and append-only JSONL log.
- [scratch](https://docs.rs/scratch/index.html)
- Scratch/candidate store: content-addressed `.zen`snapshots indexed in`scratch/index.jsonl`.
- [session](https://docs.rs/session/index.html)
- Tier-1 ephemeral session: a content-addressed snapshot DAG with a HEAD
pointer and a redo stack, persisted under `session_dir(doc_id)`.
- [store](https://docs.rs/store/index.html)
- Content-addressed object store.
- [tier2](https://docs.rs/tier2/index.html)
- Tier-2 durable version history: a bounded, flat list of state snapshots in
`versions.jsonl`(the “light git per file” — a Google-Docs-style version panel, NOT a full VCS: no branches/merge). Each version is a full content snapshot (content-addressed); named versions carry a label. Restore returns a past version’s content for the caller to write back to the`.zen`.

# dbsp - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/dbsp/0.316.0/dbsp/

## Expand description

The `dbsp` crate implements a computational engine for continuous analysis
of changing data.  With DBSP, a programmer writes code in terms of
computations on a complete data set, but DBSP implements it incrementally,
meaning that changes to the data set run in time proportional to the size of
the change rather than the size of the data set.  This is a major advantage
for applications that work with large data sets that change frequently in
small ways.

The [ tutorial](https://docs.rs/tutorial/index.html) is a good place to start for a guided tour.  After that, if
you want to look through the API on your own, the

[module is a reasonable starting point. For complete examples, visit the](https://docs.rs/circuit/index.html)

`circuit`[directory in the DBSP repository.](https://github.com/feldera/feldera/tree/main/crates/dbsp/examples)

`examples`[§](https://docs.rs#theory)Theory

DBSP is underpinned by a formal theory:

-
Here is [a presentation about DBSP](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iT4k5DCnvPU)at the 2023 Apache Calcite Meetup.

The model provides two things:

-
**Semantics.**DBSP defines a formal language of streaming operators and queries built out of these operators, and precisely specifies how these queries must transform input streams to output streams.
-
**Algorithm.**DBSP also gives an algorithm that takes an arbitrary query and generates an incremental dataflow program that implements this query correctly (in accordance with its formal semantics) and efficiently. Efficiency here means, in a nutshell, that the cost of processing a set of input events is proportional to the size of the input rather than the entire state of the database.

[§](https://docs.rs#crate-overview)Crate overview

This crate consists of several layers.

-
`dynamic`
-
`typed_batch`
-
`trace`
-
`operator::dynamic`
-
`operator``operator::dynamic`

# konst 0.4.3 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/konst/0.4.3

Const equivalents of std features: comparison, destructuring, iteration, and parsing

# Features

This crate provides:

-
Const fn equivalents of standard library functions, methods, and operators.
-
`destructure``destructure_rec``if_let_Some``while_let_Some`
-
Compile-time parsing through the `Parser``parser_method`

# Examples

### Parsing an enum

This example demonstrates how you can parse a simple enum from an environment variable, at compile-time.

```
use ;
use ;
use ;
const CHOICE: &str = unwrap_or!;
const DIRECTION: Direction = unwrap!;
// `PanicFmt` derives the `PanicFmt` trait for debug-printing in `result::unwrap`.
// To use the `PanicFmt` derive you need to enable the "const_panic_derive" feature.
;
```
### Parsing CSV

This example demonstrates how CSV can be parsed into integers.

This example requires the `"iter"` feature (enabled by default).

```
use ;
assert_eq!;
const CSV: &str = "3, 8, 13, 21, 34";
static PARSED:  = collect_const!;
```
### Parsing a struct

This example demonstrates how a key-value pair format can be parsed into a struct.

This requires the `"iter"` and `"parsing_proc"` features (enabled by default).

```
use ;
use ;
const PARSED: Struct = ;
pub const
pub const
pub const
pub const
```
# Cargo features

These are the features of this crate:

-
`"iter"`(enabled by default): Enables all iteration-related items that take/return iterators,
-
`"cmp"`(enabled by default): Enables all comparison-related items, the string equality and ordering comparison functions don't require this feature.
-
`"konst_proc_macros"`(enabled by default): Enables items that use proc macros and don't require other crate features: the`destructure_rec`
-
`"parsing_proc"`(enabled by default): Enables the`"parsing"`and`konst_proc_macros`features, and enables the`parser_method``"parsing"`if the slightly longer compile times aren't a problem.
-
`"parsing"`(enabled by default): Enables the`parsing``primitive::parse_*`functions.
-
`"const_panic_derive"`(disabled by default): Enables the "derive" feature of the`const_panic`public dependency.
-
`"alloc"`(disabled by default): Enables items that use types from the`alloc`

### Rust release related

None of thse features are enabled by default.

- `"rust_latest_stable"`: enables the latest- `"rust_1_*"`feature. Only recommendable if you can update the Rust compiler every stable release.

# No-std support

`konst` is `#![no_std]`, it can be used anywhere Rust can be used.

# Minimum Supported Rust Version

`konst` requires Rust 1.89.0.

Features that require newer versions of Rust, or the nightly compiler, need to be explicitly enabled with crate features.

# konst - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/konst/0.4.3/target-redirect/konst/

## Expand description

Const equivalents of std features: comparison, destructuring, iteration, and parsing

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

This crate provides:

-
Const fn equivalents of standard library functions, methods, and operators.
-
`destructure``destructure_rec``if_let_Some``while_let_Some`
-
Compile-time parsing through the `Parser``parser_method`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

[§](https://docs.rs#parsing-an-enum)Parsing an enum

This example demonstrates how you can parse a simple enum from an environment variable, at compile-time.

```
use konst::{eq_str, option, result};
use konst::const_panic::{self, PanicFmt};
use std::fmt::{self, Display};
const CHOICE: &str = option::unwrap_or!(option_env!("chosen-direction"), "forward");
const DIRECTION: Direction = result::unwrap!(Direction::try_parse(CHOICE));
fn main() {
    match DIRECTION {
        Direction::Forward => assert_eq!(CHOICE, "forward"),
        Direction::Backward => assert_eq!(CHOICE, "backward"),
        Direction::Left => assert_eq!(CHOICE, "left"),
        Direction::Right => assert_eq!(CHOICE, "right"),
    }
}
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
enum Direction {
    Forward,
    Backward,
    Left,
    Right,
}
impl Direction {
    const fn try_parse(input: &str) -> Result<Self, ParseDirectionError> {
        // As of Rust 1.89.0, string patterns don't work in const contexts
        match () {
            _ if eq_str(input, "forward") => Ok(Direction::Forward),
            _ if eq_str(input, "backward") => Ok(Direction::Backward),
            _ if eq_str(input, "left") => Ok(Direction::Left),
            _ if eq_str(input, "right") => Ok(Direction::Right),
            _ => Err(ParseDirectionError),
        }
    }
}
// `PanicFmt` derives the `PanicFmt` trait for debug-printing in `result::unwrap`.
// To use the `PanicFmt` derive you need to enable the "const_panic_derive" feature.
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, PanicFmt)]
pub struct ParseDirectionError;
impl Display for ParseDirectionError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        f.write_str("Failed to parse a Direction")
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#parsing-csv)Parsing CSV

This example demonstrates how CSV can be parsed into integers.

This example requires the `"iter"` feature (enabled by default).

```
use konst::{iter, result, string};
assert_eq!(PARSED, [3, 8, 13, 21, 34]);
const CSV: &str = "3, 8, 13, 21, 34";
static PARSED: [u64; 5] = iter::collect_const!(u64 =>
    string::split(CSV, ","),
        map(str::trim_ascii),
        map(|s| result::unwrap!(u64::from_str_radix(s, 10))),
);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#parsing-a-struct)Parsing a struct

This example demonstrates how a key-value pair format can be parsed into a struct.

This requires the `"iter"` and `"parsing_proc"` features (enabled by default).

```
use konst::{result, try_};
use konst::parsing::{Parser, ParseError, parser_method};
fn main(){
    assert_eq!(
        PARSED,
        Struct{
            name: "bob smith",
            amount: 1000,
            repeating: Shape::Circle,
            colors: [Color::Red, Color::Blue, Color::Green, Color::Blue],
        }
    );
}
const PARSED: Struct = {
    // You can also parse strings from environment variables, or from an `include_str!(....)`
    let input = "\
        colors = red, blue, green, blue
        amount = 1000
        repeating = circle
        name = bob smith
    ";

    result::unwrap!(parse_struct(&mut Parser::new(input)))
};
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Struct<'a> {
    pub name: &'a str,
    pub amount: usize,
    pub repeating: Shape,
    pub colors: [Color; 4],
}
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Shape {
    Circle,
    Square,
    Line,
}
#[derive(Debug, Copy, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Color {
    Red,
    Blue,
    Green,
}
pub const fn parse_struct<'p>(parser: &mut Parser<'p>) -> Result<Struct<'p>, ParseError<'p>> {
    let mut name = "<none>";
    let mut amount = 0;
    let mut repeating = Shape::Circle;
    let mut colors = [Color::Red; 4];

    parser.trim_end();
    if !parser.is_empty() {
        loop {
            // keeps a copy of the parser at this position to parse the field name
            let mut prev_parser = parser.trim_start().copy();
            // skip past the `=` to parse the field value
            try_!(parser.find_skip('=')).trim_start();
            parser_method!{prev_parser, strip_prefix;
                "name" => name = try_!(parser.split_keep('\n')),
                "amount" => amount = try_!(parser.parse_usize()),
                "repeating" => repeating = try_!(parse_shape(parser)),
                "colors" => colors = try_!(parse_colors(parser)),
                _ => {
                    let err = &"could not parse Struct field name";
                    return Err(prev_parser.to_other_error(err));
                }
            }
            if parser.is_empty() {
                break
            }
            try_!(parser.strip_prefix("\n"));
        }
    }
    Ok(Struct{name, amount, repeating, colors})
}
pub const fn parse_shape<'p>(parser: &mut Parser<'p>) -> Result<Shape, ParseError<'p>> {
    let shape = parser_method!{parser, strip_prefix;
        "circle" => Shape::Circle,
        "square" => Shape::Square,
        "line" => Shape::Line,
        _ => return Err(parser.to_other_error(&"could not parse Shape"))
    };
    Ok(shape)
}
pub const fn parse_colors<'p, const LEN: usize>(
    parser: &mut Parser<'p>,
) -> Result<[Color; LEN], ParseError<'p>> {
    let mut colors = konst::array::ArrayBuilder::of_copy();
    while !colors.is_full() {
        colors.push(try_!(parse_color(parser.trim_start())));

        // returns an error if there aren't enough comma-separated colors
        if let Err(e) = parser.strip_prefix(",") && !colors.is_full() {
            return Err(e);
        }
    }
    Ok(colors.build())
}
pub const fn parse_color<'p>(parser: &mut Parser<'p>) -> Result<Color, ParseError<'p>> {
    let color = parser_method!{parser, strip_prefix;
        "red" => Color::Red,
        "blue" => Color::Blue,
        "green" => Color::Green,
        _ => return Err(parser.to_other_error(&"could not parse Color"))
    };
    Ok(color)
}
```

# konst - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/konst/0.4.3/konst/index.html

## Expand description

Const equivalents of std features: comparison, destructuring, iteration, and parsing

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

This crate provides:

-
Const fn equivalents of standard library functions, methods, and operators.
-
`destructure``destructure_rec``if_let_Some``while_let_Some`
-
Compile-time parsing through the `Parser``parser_method`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

[§](https://docs.rs#parsing-an-enum)Parsing an enum

This example demonstrates how you can parse a simple enum from an environment variable, at compile-time.

```
use konst::{eq_str, option, result};
use konst::const_panic::{self, PanicFmt};
use std::fmt::{self, Display};
const CHOICE: &str = option::unwrap_or!(option_env!("chosen-direction"), "forward");
const DIRECTION: Direction = result::unwrap!(Direction::try_parse(CHOICE));
fn main() {
    match DIRECTION {
        Direction::Forward => assert_eq!(CHOICE, "forward"),
        Direction::Backward => assert_eq!(CHOICE, "backward"),
        Direction::Left => assert_eq!(CHOICE, "left"),
        Direction::Right => assert_eq!(CHOICE, "right"),
    }
}
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
enum Direction {
    Forward,
    Backward,
    Left,
    Right,
}
impl Direction {
    const fn try_parse(input: &str) -> Result<Self, ParseDirectionError> {
        // As of Rust 1.89.0, string patterns don't work in const contexts
        match () {
            _ if eq_str(input, "forward") => Ok(Direction::Forward),
            _ if eq_str(input, "backward") => Ok(Direction::Backward),
            _ if eq_str(input, "left") => Ok(Direction::Left),
            _ if eq_str(input, "right") => Ok(Direction::Right),
            _ => Err(ParseDirectionError),
        }
    }
}
// `PanicFmt` derives the `PanicFmt` trait for debug-printing in `result::unwrap`.
// To use the `PanicFmt` derive you need to enable the "const_panic_derive" feature.
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, PanicFmt)]
pub struct ParseDirectionError;
impl Display for ParseDirectionError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        f.write_str("Failed to parse a Direction")
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#parsing-csv)Parsing CSV

This example demonstrates how CSV can be parsed into integers.

This example requires the `"iter"` feature (enabled by default).

```
use konst::{iter, result, string};
assert_eq!(PARSED, [3, 8, 13, 21, 34]);
const CSV: &str = "3, 8, 13, 21, 34";
static PARSED: [u64; 5] = iter::collect_const!(u64 =>
    string::split(CSV, ","),
        map(str::trim_ascii),
        map(|s| result::unwrap!(u64::from_str_radix(s, 10))),
);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#parsing-a-struct)Parsing a struct

This example demonstrates how a key-value pair format can be parsed into a struct.

This requires the `"iter"` and `"parsing_proc"` features (enabled by default).

```
use konst::{result, try_};
use konst::parsing::{Parser, ParseError, parser_method};
fn main(){
    assert_eq!(
        PARSED,
        Struct{
            name: "bob smith",
            amount: 1000,
            repeating: Shape::Circle,
            colors: [Color::Red, Color::Blue, Color::Green, Color::Blue],
        }
    );
}
const PARSED: Struct = {
    // You can also parse strings from environment variables, or from an `include_str!(....)`
    let input = "\
        colors = red, blue, green, blue
        amount = 1000
        repeating = circle
        name = bob smith
    ";

    result::unwrap!(parse_struct(&mut Parser::new(input)))
};
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Struct<'a> {
    pub name: &'a str,
    pub amount: usize,
    pub repeating: Shape,
    pub colors: [Color; 4],
}
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Shape {
    Circle,
    Square,
    Line,
}
#[derive(Debug, Copy, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Color {
    Red,
    Blue,
    Green,
}
pub const fn parse_struct<'p>(parser: &mut Parser<'p>) -> Result<Struct<'p>, ParseError<'p>> {
    let mut name = "<none>";
    let mut amount = 0;
    let mut repeating = Shape::Circle;
    let mut colors = [Color::Red; 4];

    parser.trim_end();
    if !parser.is_empty() {
        loop {
            // keeps a copy of the parser at this position to parse the field name
            let mut prev_parser = parser.trim_start().copy();
            // skip past the `=` to parse the field value
            try_!(parser.find_skip('=')).trim_start();
            parser_method!{prev_parser, strip_prefix;
                "name" => name = try_!(parser.split_keep('\n')),
                "amount" => amount = try_!(parser.parse_usize()),
                "repeating" => repeating = try_!(parse_shape(parser)),
                "colors" => colors = try_!(parse_colors(parser)),
                _ => {
                    let err = &"could not parse Struct field name";
                    return Err(prev_parser.to_other_error(err));
                }
            }
            if parser.is_empty() {
                break
            }
            try_!(parser.strip_prefix("\n"));
        }
    }
    Ok(Struct{name, amount, repeating, colors})
}
pub const fn parse_shape<'p>(parser: &mut Parser<'p>) -> Result<Shape, ParseError<'p>> {
    let shape = parser_method!{parser, strip_prefix;
        "circle" => Shape::Circle,
        "square" => Shape::Square,
        "line" => Shape::Line,
        _ => return Err(parser.to_other_error(&"could not parse Shape"))
    };
    Ok(shape)
}
pub const fn parse_colors<'p, const LEN: usize>(
    parser: &mut Parser<'p>,
) -> Result<[Color; LEN], ParseError<'p>> {
    let mut colors = konst::array::ArrayBuilder::of_copy();
    while !colors.is_full() {
        colors.push(try_!(parse_color(parser.trim_start())));

        // returns an error if there aren't enough comma-separated colors
        if let Err(e) = parser.strip_prefix(",") && !colors.is_full() {
            return Err(e);
        }
    }
    Ok(colors.build())
}
pub const fn parse_color<'p>(parser: &mut Parser<'p>) -> Result<Color, ParseError<'p>> {
    let color = parser_method!{parser, strip_prefix;
        "red" => Color::Red,
        "blue" => Color::Blue,
        "green" => Color::Green,
        _ => return Err(parser.to_other_error(&"could not parse Color"))
    };
    Ok(color)
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#cargo-features)Cargo features

These are the features of this crate:

-
`"iter"`(enabled by default): Enables all iteration-related items that take/return iterators,
-
`"cmp"`(enabled by default): Enables all comparison-related items, the string equality and ordering comparison functions don’t require this feature.
-
`"konst_proc_macros"`(enabled by default): Enables items that use proc macros and don’t require other crate features: the`destructure_rec`
-
`"parsing_proc"`(enabled by default): Enables the`"parsing"`and`konst_proc_macros`features, and enables the`parser_method``"parsing"`if the slightly longer compile times aren’t a problem.
-
`"parsing"`(enabled by default): Enables the`parsing``primitive::parse_*`functions.
-
`"const_panic_derive"`(disabled by default): Enables the “derive” feature of the`const_panic`public dependency.
-
`"alloc"`(disabled by default): Enables items that use types from the`alloc`

[§](https://docs.rs#rust-release-related)Rust release related

None of thse features are enabled by default.

- `"rust_latest_stable"`: enables the latest- `"rust_1_*"`feature. Only recommendable if you can update the Rust compiler every stable release.

[§](https://docs.rs#no-std-support)No-std support

`konst` is `#![no_std]`, it can be used anywhere Rust can be used.

[§](https://docs.rs#minimum-supported-rust-version)Minimum Supported Rust Version

`konst` requires Rust 1.89.0.

Features that require newer versions of Rust, or the nightly compiler, need to be explicitly enabled with crate features.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [assertc_](https://docs.rs/macro.assertc_eq.html)- eq - `cmp`
- For asserting that two values are equal.
- [assertc_](https://docs.rs/macro.assertc_ne.html)- ne - `cmp`
- For asserting that two values are unequal.
- [destructure](https://docs.rs/macro.destructure.html)
- Destructures a struct/tuple/array into all of its elements/fields.
- [destructure_](https://docs.rs/macro.destructure_rec.html)- rec - `konst_proc_macros`
- Nested destructuring of structs/tuples/arrays (composite types).
- [for_](https://docs.rs/macro.for_range.html)- range
- For loop over a range
- [if_](https://docs.rs/macro.if_let_Some.html)- let_ - Some
- Emulates by-value destructuring of a `Some`
- [try_](https://docs.rs/macro.try_.html)
- `?`-like macro for- `Result`
- [try_opt](https://docs.rs/macro.try_opt.html)
- `?`-like macro for- `Option`s.
- [while_](https://docs.rs/macro.while_let_Some.html)- let_ - Some
- Emulates a by-value `while let Some`loop over`Drop`-type-containing`Option`s in const.

# lib.rs - source

Source: https://docs.rs/konst/0.4.3/src/konst/lib.rs.html

# konst/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)//! Const equivalents of std features: comparison, destructuring, iteration, and parsing
[2](https://docs.rs#2)//!
[3](https://docs.rs#3)//! # Features
[4](https://docs.rs#4)//!
[5](https://docs.rs#5)//! This crate provides:
[6](https://docs.rs#6)//!
[7](https://docs.rs#7)//! - Const fn equivalents of standard library functions, methods, and operators.
[8](https://docs.rs#8)//!
[9](https://docs.rs#9)//! - [Const iterators].
[10](https://docs.rs#10)//!
[11](https://docs.rs#11)//! - [`destructure`]/[`destructure_rec`]/[`if_let_Some`]/[`while_let_Some`]
[12](https://docs.rs#12)//! macros to allow destructuring types in const without getting "cannot drop in const" errors.
[13](https://docs.rs#13)//!
[14](https://docs.rs#14)//! - Compile-time parsing through the [`Parser`] type, and [`parser_method`] macro.
[15](https://docs.rs#15)//!
[16](https://docs.rs#16)//! # Examples
[17](https://docs.rs#17)//!
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//! ### Parsing an enum
[19](https://docs.rs#19)//!
[20](https://docs.rs#20)//! This example demonstrates how you can parse a simple enum from an environment variable,
[21](https://docs.rs#21)//! at compile-time.
[22](https://docs.rs#22)//!
[23](https://docs.rs#23)//! ```rust
[24](https://docs.rs#24)//! use konst::{eq_str, option, result};
[25](https://docs.rs#25)//! use konst::const_panic::{self, PanicFmt};
[26](https://docs.rs#26)//!
[27](https://docs.rs#27)//! use std::fmt::{self, Display};
[28](https://docs.rs#28)//!
[29](https://docs.rs#29)//!
[30](https://docs.rs#30)//! const CHOICE: &str = option::unwrap_or!(option_env!("chosen-direction"), "forward");
[31](https://docs.rs#31)//!
[32](https://docs.rs#32)//! const DIRECTION: Direction = result::unwrap!(Direction::try_parse(CHOICE));
[33](https://docs.rs#33)//!
[34](https://docs.rs#34)//! fn main() {
[35](https://docs.rs#35)//!     match DIRECTION {
[36](https://docs.rs#36)//!         Direction::Forward => assert_eq!(CHOICE, "forward"),
[37](https://docs.rs#37)//!         Direction::Backward => assert_eq!(CHOICE, "backward"),
[38](https://docs.rs#38)//!         Direction::Left => assert_eq!(CHOICE, "left"),
[39](https://docs.rs#39)//!         Direction::Right => assert_eq!(CHOICE, "right"),
[40](https://docs.rs#40)//!     }
[41](https://docs.rs#41)//! }
[42](https://docs.rs#42)//!
[43](https://docs.rs#43)//!
[44](https://docs.rs#44)//! #[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
[45](https://docs.rs#45)//! enum Direction {
[46](https://docs.rs#46)//!     Forward,
[47](https://docs.rs#47)//!     Backward,
[48](https://docs.rs#48)//!     Left,
[49](https://docs.rs#49)//!     Right,
[50](https://docs.rs#50)//! }
[51](https://docs.rs#51)//!
[52](https://docs.rs#52)//! impl Direction {
[53](https://docs.rs#53)//!     const fn try_parse(input: &str) -> Result<Self, ParseDirectionError> {
[54](https://docs.rs#54)//!         // As of Rust 1.89.0, string patterns don't work in const contexts
[55](https://docs.rs#55)//!         match () {
[56](https://docs.rs#56)//!             _ if eq_str(input, "forward") => Ok(Direction::Forward),
[57](https://docs.rs#57)//!             _ if eq_str(input, "backward") => Ok(Direction::Backward),
[58](https://docs.rs#58)//!             _ if eq_str(input, "left") => Ok(Direction::Left),
[59](https://docs.rs#59)//!             _ if eq_str(input, "right") => Ok(Direction::Right),
[60](https://docs.rs#60)//!             _ => Err(ParseDirectionError),
[61](https://docs.rs#61)//!         }
[62](https://docs.rs#62)//!     }
[63](https://docs.rs#63)//! }
[64](https://docs.rs#64)//!
[65](https://docs.rs#65)//! // `PanicFmt` derives the `PanicFmt` trait for debug-printing in `result::unwrap`.
[66](https://docs.rs#66)//! // To use the `PanicFmt` derive you need to enable the "const_panic_derive" feature.
[67](https://docs.rs#67)//! #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, PanicFmt)]
[68](https://docs.rs#68)//! pub struct ParseDirectionError;
[69](https://docs.rs#69)//!
[70](https://docs.rs#70)//! impl Display for ParseDirectionError {
[71](https://docs.rs#71)//!     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
[72](https://docs.rs#72)//!         f.write_str("Failed to parse a Direction")
[73](https://docs.rs#73)//!     }
[74](https://docs.rs#74)//! }
[75](https://docs.rs#75)//! ```
[76](https://docs.rs#76)//!
[77](https://docs.rs#77)//! ### Parsing CSV
[78](https://docs.rs#78)//!
[79](https://docs.rs#79)//! This example demonstrates how CSV can be parsed into integers.
[80](https://docs.rs#80)//!
[81](https://docs.rs#81)//! This example requires the `"iter"` feature (enabled by default).
[82](https://docs.rs#82)//!
[83](https://docs.rs#83)#![cfg_attr(feature = "iter", doc = "```rust")]
[84](https://docs.rs#84)#![cfg_attr(not(feature = "iter"), doc = "```ignore")]
[85](https://docs.rs#85)//! use konst::{iter, result, string};
[86](https://docs.rs#86)//!
[87](https://docs.rs#87)//!
[88](https://docs.rs#88)//! assert_eq!(PARSED, [3, 8, 13, 21, 34]);
[89](https://docs.rs#89)//!
[90](https://docs.rs#90)//!
[91](https://docs.rs#91)//! const CSV: &str = "3, 8, 13, 21, 34";
[92](https://docs.rs#92)//!
[93](https://docs.rs#93)//! static PARSED: [u64; 5] = iter::collect_const!(u64 =>
[94](https://docs.rs#94)//!     string::split(CSV, ","),
[95](https://docs.rs#95)//!         map(str::trim_ascii),
[96](https://docs.rs#96)//!         map(|s| result::unwrap!(u64::from_str_radix(s, 10))),
[97](https://docs.rs#97)//! );
[98](https://docs.rs#98)//! ```
[99](https://docs.rs#99)//!
[100](https://docs.rs#100)//! ### Parsing a struct
[101](https://docs.rs#101)//!
[102](https://docs.rs#102)//! This example demonstrates how a key-value pair format can be parsed into a struct.
[103](https://docs.rs#103)//!
[104](https://docs.rs#104)//! This requires the `"iter"` and `"parsing_proc"` features (enabled by default).
[105](https://docs.rs#105)//!
[106](https://docs.rs#106)#![cfg_attr(all(feature = "iter", feature = "parsing_proc"), doc = "```rust")]
[107](https://docs.rs#107)#![cfg_attr(
[108](https://docs.rs#108)    not(all(feature = "iter", feature = "parsing_proc")),
[109](https://docs.rs#109)    doc = "```ignore"
[110](https://docs.rs#110))]
[111](https://docs.rs#111)//! use konst::{result, try_};
[112](https://docs.rs#112)//! use konst::parsing::{Parser, ParseError, parser_method};
[113](https://docs.rs#113)//!
[114](https://docs.rs#114)//!
[115](https://docs.rs#115)//! fn main(){
[116](https://docs.rs#116)//!     assert_eq!(
[117](https://docs.rs#117)//!         PARSED,
[118](https://docs.rs#118)//!         Struct{
[119](https://docs.rs#119)//!             name: "bob smith",
[120](https://docs.rs#120)//!             amount: 1000,
[121](https://docs.rs#121)//!             repeating: Shape::Circle,
[122](https://docs.rs#122)//!             colors: [Color::Red, Color::Blue, Color::Green, Color::Blue],
[123](https://docs.rs#123)//!         }
[124](https://docs.rs#124)//!     );
[125](https://docs.rs#125)//! }
[126](https://docs.rs#126)//!
[127](https://docs.rs#127)//!
[128](https://docs.rs#128)//! const PARSED: Struct = {
[129](https://docs.rs#129)//!     // You can also parse strings from environment variables, or from an `include_str!(....)`
[130](https://docs.rs#130)//!     let input = "\
[131](https://docs.rs#131)//!         colors = red, blue, green, blue
[132](https://docs.rs#132)//!         amount = 1000
[133](https://docs.rs#133)//!         repeating = circle
[134](https://docs.rs#134)//!         name = bob smith
[135](https://docs.rs#135)//!     ";
[136](https://docs.rs#136)//!
[137](https://docs.rs#137)//!     result::unwrap!(parse_struct(&mut Parser::new(input)))
[138](https://docs.rs#138)//! };
[139](https://docs.rs#139)//!
[140](https://docs.rs#140)//! #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
[141](https://docs.rs#141)//! pub struct Struct<'a> {
[142](https://docs.rs#142)//!     pub name: &'a str,
[143](https://docs.rs#143)//!     pub amount: usize,
[144](https://docs.rs#144)//!     pub repeating: Shape,
[145](https://docs.rs#145)//!     pub colors: [Color; 4],
[146](https://docs.rs#146)//! }
[147](https://docs.rs#147)//!
[148](https://docs.rs#148)//! #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
[149](https://docs.rs#149)//! pub enum Shape {
[150](https://docs.rs#150)//!     Circle,
[151](https://docs.rs#151)//!     Square,
[152](https://docs.rs#152)//!     Line,
[153](https://docs.rs#153)//! }
[154](https://docs.rs#154)//!
[155](https://docs.rs#155)//! #[derive(Debug, Copy, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
[156](https://docs.rs#156)//! pub enum Color {
[157](https://docs.rs#157)//!     Red,
[158](https://docs.rs#158)//!     Blue,
[159](https://docs.rs#159)//!     Green,
[160](https://docs.rs#160)//! }
[161](https://docs.rs#161)//!
[162](https://docs.rs#162)//! pub const fn parse_struct<'p>(parser: &mut Parser<'p>) -> Result<Struct<'p>, ParseError<'p>> {
[163](https://docs.rs#163)//!     let mut name = "<none>";
[164](https://docs.rs#164)//!     let mut amount = 0;
[165](https://docs.rs#165)//!     let mut repeating = Shape::Circle;
[166](https://docs.rs#166)//!     let mut colors = [Color::Red; 4];
[167](https://docs.rs#167)//!
[168](https://docs.rs#168)//!     parser.trim_end();
[169](https://docs.rs#169)//!     if !parser.is_empty() {
[170](https://docs.rs#170)//!         loop {
[171](https://docs.rs#171)//!             // keeps a copy of the parser at this position to parse the field name
[172](https://docs.rs#172)//!             let mut prev_parser = parser.trim_start().copy();
[173](https://docs.rs#173)//!
[174](https://docs.rs#174)//!             // skip past the `=` to parse the field value
[175](https://docs.rs#175)//!             try_!(parser.find_skip('=')).trim_start();
[176](https://docs.rs#176)//!
[177](https://docs.rs#177)//!             parser_method!{prev_parser, strip_prefix;
[178](https://docs.rs#178)//!                 "name" => name = try_!(parser.split_keep('\n')),
[179](https://docs.rs#179)//!                 "amount" => amount = try_!(parser.parse_usize()),
[180](https://docs.rs#180)//!                 "repeating" => repeating = try_!(parse_shape(parser)),
[181](https://docs.rs#181)//!                 "colors" => colors = try_!(parse_colors(parser)),
[182](https://docs.rs#182)//!                 _ => {
[183](https://docs.rs#183)//!                     let err = &"could not parse Struct field name";
[184](https://docs.rs#184)//!                     return Err(prev_parser.to_other_error(err));
[185](https://docs.rs#185)//!                 }
[186](https://docs.rs#186)//!             }
[187](https://docs.rs#187)//!
[188](https://docs.rs#188)//!             if parser.is_empty() {
[189](https://docs.rs#189)//!                 break
[190](https://docs.rs#190)//!             }
[191](https://docs.rs#191)//!             try_!(parser.strip_prefix("\n"));
[192](https://docs.rs#192)//!         }
[193](https://docs.rs#193)//!     }
[194](https://docs.rs#194)//!
[195](https://docs.rs#195)//!     Ok(Struct{name, amount, repeating, colors})
[196](https://docs.rs#196)//! }
[197](https://docs.rs#197)//!
[198](https://docs.rs#198)//! pub const fn parse_shape<'p>(parser: &mut Parser<'p>) -> Result<Shape, ParseError<'p>> {
[199](https://docs.rs#199)//!     let shape = parser_method!{parser, strip_prefix;
[200](https://docs.rs#200)//!         "circle" => Shape::Circle,
[201](https://docs.rs#201)//!         "square" => Shape::Square,
[202](https://docs.rs#202)//!         "line" => Shape::Line,
[203](https://docs.rs#203)//!         _ => return Err(parser.to_other_error(&"could not parse Shape"))
[204](https://docs.rs#204)//!     };
[205](https://docs.rs#205)//!     Ok(shape)
[206](https://docs.rs#206)//! }
[207](https://docs.rs#207)//!
[208](https://docs.rs#208)//! pub const fn parse_colors<'p, const LEN: usize>(
[209](https://docs.rs#209)//!     parser: &mut Parser<'p>,
[210](https://docs.rs#210)//! ) -> Result<[Color; LEN], ParseError<'p>> {
[211](https://docs.rs#211)//!     let mut colors = konst::array::ArrayBuilder::of_copy();
[212](https://docs.rs#212)//!
[213](https://docs.rs#213)//!     while !colors.is_full() {
[214](https://docs.rs#214)//!         colors.push(try_!(parse_color(parser.trim_start())));
[215](https://docs.rs#215)//!
[216](https://docs.rs#216)//!         // returns an error if there aren't enough comma-separated colors
[217](https://docs.rs#217)//!         if let Err(e) = parser.strip_prefix(",") && !colors.is_full() {
[218](https://docs.rs#218)//!             return Err(e);
[219](https://docs.rs#219)//!         }
[220](https://docs.rs#220)//!     }
[221](https://docs.rs#221)//!
[222](https://docs.rs#222)//!     Ok(colors.build())
[223](https://docs.rs#223)//! }
[224](https://docs.rs#224)//!
[225](https://docs.rs#225)//! pub const fn parse_color<'p>(parser: &mut Parser<'p>) -> Result<Color, ParseError<'p>> {
[226](https://docs.rs#226)//!     let color = parser_method!{parser, strip_prefix;
[227](https://docs.rs#227)//!         "red" => Color::Red,
[228](https://docs.rs#228)//!         "blue" => Color::Blue,
[229](https://docs.rs#229)//!         "green" => Color::Green,
[230](https://docs.rs#230)//!         _ => return Err(parser.to_other_error(&"could not parse Color"))
[231](https://docs.rs#231)//!     };
[232](https://docs.rs#232)//!     Ok(color)
[233](https://docs.rs#233)//! }
[234](https://docs.rs#234)//!
[235](https://docs.rs#235)//! ```
[236](https://docs.rs#236)//!
[237](https://docs.rs#237)//! # Cargo features
[238](https://docs.rs#238)//!
[239](https://docs.rs#239)//! These are the features of this crate:
[240](https://docs.rs#240)//!
[241](https://docs.rs#241)//! - `"iter"`(enabled by default):
[242](https://docs.rs#242)//! Enables all iteration-related items that take/return iterators,
[243](https://docs.rs#243)//!
[244](https://docs.rs#244)//! - `"cmp"`(enabled by default):
[245](https://docs.rs#245)//! Enables all comparison-related items,
[246](https://docs.rs#246)//! the string equality and ordering comparison functions don't require this feature.
[247](https://docs.rs#247)//!
[248](https://docs.rs#248)//! - `"konst_proc_macros"`(enabled by default):
[249](https://docs.rs#249)//! Enables items that use proc macros and don't require other crate features:
[250](https://docs.rs#250)//! the [`destructure_rec`] macro.
[251](https://docs.rs#251)//!
[252](https://docs.rs#252)//! - `"parsing_proc"`(enabled by default):
[253](https://docs.rs#253)//! Enables the `"parsing"` and `konst_proc_macros` features,
[254](https://docs.rs#254)//! and enables the [`parser_method`] macro.
[255](https://docs.rs#255)//! You can use this feature instead of `"parsing"` if the slightly longer
[256](https://docs.rs#256)//! compile times aren't a problem.
[257](https://docs.rs#257)//!
[258](https://docs.rs#258)//! - `"parsing"`(enabled by default):
[259](https://docs.rs#259)//! Enables the [`parsing`] module for parsing from strings,
[260](https://docs.rs#260)//! and the `primitive::parse_*` functions.
[261](https://docs.rs#261)//!
[262](https://docs.rs#262)//! - `"const_panic_derive"`(disabled by default):
[263](https://docs.rs#263)//! Enables the "derive" feature of the `const_panic` public dependency.
[264](https://docs.rs#264)//!
[265](https://docs.rs#265)//! - `"alloc"`(disabled by default):
[266](https://docs.rs#266)//! Enables items that use types from the [`alloc`] crate.
[267](https://docs.rs#267)//!
[268](https://docs.rs#268)//! ### Rust release related
[269](https://docs.rs#269)//!

# konst::iter - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/konst/0.4.3/konst/iter/index.html

Available on

**crate feature**only.`iter`## Expand description

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use crate::polymorphism::kinds::`- [IsIntoIterKind](https://docs.rs/polymorphism/kinds/enum.IsIntoIterKind.html);
- `pub use crate::polymorphism::kinds::`- [IsIteratorKind](https://docs.rs/polymorphism/kinds/enum.IsIteratorKind.html);
- `pub use crate::polymorphism::kinds::`- [IsStdKind](https://docs.rs/polymorphism/kinds/enum.IsStdKind.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [iterator_](https://docs.rs/iterator_dsl/index.html)- dsl
- Documentation on the iterator DSL that some `konst::iter`macros support.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [collect_](https://docs.rs/macro.collect_const.html)- const
- Collects an iterator constant into an array
- [eval](https://docs.rs/macro.eval.html)
- Emulates iterator method chains, by expanding to equivalent code.
- [for_](https://docs.rs/macro.for_each.html)- each
- Iterates over all elements of an [iterator](https://docs.rs/trait.ConstIntoIter.html), const equivalent of`Iterator::for_each`
- [into_](https://docs.rs/macro.into_iter.html)- iter
- Macro for converting `ConstIntoIter`

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Into](https://docs.rs/struct.IntoIterWrapper.html)- Iter - Wrapper
- Wrapper for `ConstIntoIter`implementors, that defines different methods depending on the value of`K`.
- [Repeat](https://docs.rs/struct.Repeat.html)
- Const analog of `core::iter::Repeat``repeat`
- [RepeatN](https://docs.rs/struct.RepeatN.html)
- Const analog of `core::iter::RepeatN``repeat_n`

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Const](https://docs.rs/trait.ConstIntoIter.html)- Into - Iter
- Const analog of the `IntoIterator`
- [Const](https://docs.rs/trait.ConstIntoIterKind.html)- Into - Iter - Kind
- Trait for the types that are assignable to `ConstIntoIter::Kind`
- [Step](https://docs.rs/trait.Step.html)
- Trait for all the types that ranges can iterate over.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [coerce](https://docs.rs/fn.coerce.html)
- Coerces the argument to a type that has a `.const_into_iter()`method
- [repeat](https://docs.rs/fn.repeat.html)
- Const analog of `core::iter::repeat``Copy`(instead of`Clone`).
- [repeat_](https://docs.rs/fn.repeat_n.html)- n
- Const analog of `core::iter::repeat_n``Copy`(instead of`Clone`).

# destructure in konst - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/konst/0.4.3/konst/macro.destructure.html

```
macro_rules! destructure {
    ($($(@$is_path:tt)? ::)? $($path:ident)::+ $(,)?{$($braced:tt)*} $($rem:tt)*) => { ... };
    ($($(@$is_path:tt)? ::)? $($path:ident)::+ $(,)? ($($tupled:tt)*) $($rem:tt)*) => { ... };
    ($struct_path:path $(,)? {$($braced:tt)*} $($rem:tt)*) => { ... };
    ($struct_path:path, ($($tupled:tt)*) $($rem:tt)*) => { ... };
    (() $(:$tuple_ty:ty)? = $val:expr) => { ... };
    (($($tupled:tt)*) $($rem:tt)*) => { ... };
    ([] $(:$array_ty:ty)? = $val:expr) => { ... };
    (
        [$( $pat:tt $(@ $dotdot:tt)? ),* $(,)?]
        $($rem:tt)*
    ) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Destructures a struct/tuple/array into all of its elements/fields.

Use this macro over [ destructure_rec](https://docs.rs/macro.destructure_rec.html) if you only
need to destructure composite types
into

*shallow*fields of types that may need dropping. (

[requires the](https://docs.rs/macro.destructure_rec.html)

`destructure_rec``konst_proc_macros` feature,
which is enabled by default)[§](https://docs.rs#motivation)Motivation

This macro works around a limitation of Rust as of 1.89,
where in a const context, a non-`Drop` type can’t be destructured into its elements/fields
if any of them is `Drop`.

Even simple cases like this don’t compile:

```
error[E0493]: destructor of `(T, T)` cannot be evaluated at compile-time
 --> konst/src/macros/destructuring.rs:142:17
  |
3 | const fn foo<T>((a, b): (T, T)) -> [T; 2] {
  |                 ^^^^^^ the destructor for this type cannot be evaluated in constant functions
4 |     [a, b]
5 | }
  | - value is dropped here
```
[§](https://docs.rs#requirementslimitations)Requirements/Limitations

This macro has these requirements and limitations:

- it does not support `..`patterns in tuples or structs (because unmentioned fields would be leaked), but`..`patterns are supported in arrays.
- it requires that passed-in structs do not impl `Drop`(like built-in destructuring does), but any field can impl`Drop`.
- it needs to be invoked multiple times
to destructure nested structs/tuples/arrays that have `Drop`elements/fields.[(example)](https://docs.rs#nested-destructuring)
- it only supports tuple structs and tuples up to 16 elements (inclusive)

[§](https://docs.rs#syntax)Syntax

This section uses a pseudo-macro_rules syntax for each type of input.

[§](https://docs.rs#braced-structs)Braced structs

```
$struct_path:brace_path {$($field:tt $(: $pattern:pat)?),* $(,)?}
$(:$struct_ty:ty)?
= $val:expr
```
Where `:brace_path` can be either of:

- `$(::)? $($path:ident)::* $(,)?`
- `$struct_path:path $(,)?`

[§](https://docs.rs#tuple-structs)Tuple structs

```
$struct_path:tuple_path ( $($pattern:pat),* $(,)? )
$(:$struct_ty:ty)?
= $val:expr
```
Where `:tuple_path` can be either of:

- `$(::)? $($path:ident)::* $(,)?`
- `$struct_path:path ,`(braced struct patterns don’t need the- `,`)

[§](https://docs.rs#tuples)Tuples

`( $($pattern:pat),* $(,)? ) $(:$tuple_ty:ty)? = $val:expr`[§](https://docs.rs#arrays)Arrays

`[$( $pat:elem_pat $(@ ..)? ),* $(,)?] $(:$array_ty:ty)? = $val:expr`Where `:elem_pat` can be any of:

- `_`
- `..`
- `$ident:ident`
- `($pattern:pat)`: any pattern inside of parentheses

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

The functions in these examples demonstrate destructuring non-Copy types in const, which can’t be done with built-in destructuring as of Rust 1.91.

[§](https://docs.rs#braced-struct)Braced Struct

```
use std::ops::Range;
assert_eq!(PAIR, (3, 5));
const PAIR: (u32, u32) = range_to_pair(3..5);
const fn range_to_pair<T>(range: Range<T>) -> (T, T) {
    konst::destructure!{Range{start, end} = range}
    (start, end)
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#tuple-struct)Tuple Struct

```
assert_eq!(PAIR, [8, 13]);
const PAIR: [u32; 2] = Pair(8, 13).into_inner();
struct Pair<T>(T, T);
impl<T> Pair<T> {
    const fn into_inner(self) -> [T; 2] {
        konst::destructure!{Self(first, second) = self}

        [first, second]
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#tuple)Tuple

```
assert_eq!(PAIR, (5, String::new()));
const PAIR: (u32, String) = swap_pair((String::new(), 5));
const fn swap_pair<T, U>(pair: (T, U)) -> (U, T) {
    konst::destructure!{(a, b) = pair}
    (b, a)
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#array)Array

```
assert_eq!(SPLIT, (Some(String::new()), [None, None, Some(String::new())]));
const SPLIT: (Option<String>, [Option<String>; 3]) =
    split_first([Some(String::new()), None, None, Some(String::new())]);
const fn split_first<T>(array: [T; 4]) -> (T, [T; 3]) {
    konst::destructure!{[a, rem @ ..] = array}

    (a, rem)
}
```

---

# destructure_rec in konst - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/konst/0.4.3/konst/macro.destructure_rec.html

```
macro_rules! destructure_rec {
    ($($tt:tt)*) => { ... };
}
```
**crate feature**only.

`konst_proc_macros`## Expand description

Nested destructuring of structs/tuples/arrays (composite types).

Use this macro over [ destructure](https://docs.rs/macro.destructure.html) if you need to destructure composite types
into

*nested*fields that may need dropping.

[§](https://docs.rs#motivation)Motivation

This macro works around a limitation of Rust as of 1.91,
where in a const context, a non-`Drop` type can’t be destructured into its elements/fields
if any of them is `Drop`.

Even simple cases like this don’t compile:

```
error[E0493]: destructor of `((T, T), T)` cannot be evaluated at compile-time
 --> src/lib.rs:1:17
  |
1 | const fn foo<T>(((a, b), c): ((T, T), T)) -> [T; 3] {
  |                 ^^^^^^^^^^^ the destructor for this type cannot be evaluated in constant functions
2 |     [a, b, c]
3 | }
  | - value is dropped here
```
[§](https://docs.rs#requirementslimitations)Requirements/Limitations

This macro has these requirements and limitations:

- it only supports `..`patterns in tuples or structs when the`#[forget_ignored_fields]`attribute is used, which forgets unmentioned fields. (arrays always support the`..`pattern, dropping unmentioned elements)
- it requires that passed-in structs do not impl `Drop`(like built-in destructuring does).
- it always moves the expression on the right-hand-side, even if the pattern doesn’t require it.

[§](https://docs.rs#syntax)Syntax

This section describes the syntax allowed by `destructure_rec` using
`macro_rules!` syntax with pseudo-metavariable types,
the allowed syntax is

```
$(#[forget_ignored_fields])?
$pattern:dr_pat $( : $type:ty )? = $val:expr
```
`dr_pat` can be any of:

- `_ $( @ $nested_pat:dr_pat )?`
- `$(ref)? $(mut)? $ident:ident $( @ $nested_pat:dr_pat )?`
- `& $(mut)? $pat:pat`
- `$typename:path`
- `$typename:path { $($field_name:ident : $field_pat:dr_pat),* $(, ..)? $(,)? }`
- `$typename:path ( $($field_pat:dr_pat),* $(, ..)? $(,)? )`
- `[ $($pref_elem:dr_pat),* $(, $($ident:ident @)? ..)? $(, $suff_elem:dr_pat)* $(,)? ]`
- `( $($pref_elem:dr_pat),* $(, ..)? $(,)? )`

The `#[forget_ignored_fields]` attribute turns the macro from forbidding
tuple and struct patterns that use a trailing `..` to allowing
the pattern, and to cause unmentioned fields to *not* be dropped.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

The functions in these examples demonstrate destructuring non-Copy types in const, which can’t be done with built-in destructuring as of Rust 1.91.

[§](https://docs.rs#braced-struct)Braced Struct

```
use std::ops::Range;
assert_eq!(TUP, (3, 5, 8, 13));
const TUP: (u32, u32, u32, u32) = ranges_to_tuple([3..5, 8..13]);
const fn ranges_to_tuple<T>(ranges: [Range<T>; 2]) -> (T, T, T, T) {
    konst::destructure_rec!{
        [Range { start: a, end: b }, Range { start: c, end: d }] = ranges
    }
    (a, b, c, d)
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#flatten)Flatten

```
assert_eq!(FLAT, [3, 5, 8, 13]);
const FLAT: [u32; 4] = flatten([[3, 5], [8, 13]]);
const fn flatten<T>(array: [[T; 2]; 2]) -> [T; 4] {
    konst::destructure_rec!{[[a, b], [c, d]] = array}

    [a, b, c, d]
}
```

---

# if_let_Some in konst - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/konst/0.4.3/konst/macro.if_let_Some.html

```
macro_rules! if_let_Some {
    ($some:pat = $e:expr => $then:block $(else $else:block)?) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Emulates by-value destructuring of a [ Some](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.Some) variant that contains a Drop type in const.

[§](https://docs.rs#motivation)Motivation

This macro works around the fact that this code

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
const fn foo<T>(opt: Option<T>) -> Result<T, ()> {
    match opt {
        Some(x) => Ok(x),
        None => Err(())
    }
}
```
causes this error as of Rust 1.89:

```
error[E0493]: destructor of `Option<T>` cannot be evaluated at compile-time
 --> konst/src/macros/control_flow.rs:42:17
  |
3 | const fn foo<T>(opt: Option<T>) -> Result<T, ()> {
  |                 ^^^ the destructor for this type cannot be evaluated in constant functions
...
8 | }
  | - value is dropped here
```
[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
assert_eq!(ok_or_none_error(Some(10)), Ok(10));
assert_eq!(ok_or_none_error(None::<String>), Err(ItWasNoneError));
const fn ok_or_none_error<T>(opt: Option<T>) -> Result<T, ItWasNoneError> {
    konst::if_let_Some!{x = opt => {
        Ok(x)
    } else {
        Err(ItWasNoneError)
    }}
}
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct ItWasNoneError;
```

# while_let_Some in konst - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/konst/0.4.3/konst/macro.while_let_Some.html

```
macro_rules! while_let_Some {
    ($some:pat = $e:expr => $($then:tt)*) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Emulates a by-value `while let Some` loop over
`Drop`-type-containing `Option`s in const.

[§](https://docs.rs#motivation)Motivation

This macro works around the fact that this code

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use konst::array::ArrayBuilder;
const fn foo<T: SomeTrait>() -> [T; 3] {
    let mut builder = ArrayBuilder::of_drop();
    while let Some(x) = produce_option(&builder) {
        builder.push(x);
    }
    builder.build()
}
```
causes this error as of Rust 1.89:

```
error[E0493]: destructor of `Option<T>` cannot be evaluated at compile-time
  --> konst/src/macros/control_flow.rs:108:25
   |
9  |     while let Some(x) = produce_option(&builder) {
   |                         ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ the destructor for this type cannot be evaluated in constant functions
10 |         builder.push(x);
11 |     }
   |     - value is dropped here
```
[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

This example requires the `"iter"` feature (enabled by default),
because it uses [ ArrayBuilder](https://docs.rs/array/struct.ArrayBuilder.html).

```
use konst::array::ArrayBuilder;
use konst::drop_flavor::MayDrop;
assert_eq!(make_strings::<1>(), [String::new()]);
assert_eq!(make_strings::<2>(), [String::new(), String::new()]);
assert_eq!(make_strings::<3>(), [String::new(), String::new(), String::new()]);
const fn make_strings<const N: usize>() -> [String; N] {
    let mut builder = ArrayBuilder::of_drop();
    konst::while_let_Some!{x = produce_option(&builder) =>
        builder.push(x);
    }
    builder.build()
}
const fn produce_option<const N: usize>(
    ab: &ArrayBuilder<String, N, MayDrop>
) -> Option<String> {
    if ab.is_full() {
        None
    } else {
        Some(String::new())
    }
}
```

---

# Parser in konst::parsing - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/konst/0.4.3/konst/parsing/struct.Parser.html

`pub struct Parser<'a> { /* private fields */ }`**crate feature**only.

`parsing`## Expand description

For parsing and traversing over strings in const contexts.

If you’re looking for functions to parse some type from an entire string
(instead of only part of it),
then you want to look in the module for that type, eg: [ primitive](https://docs.rs/primitive/index.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

[§](https://docs.rs#parsing-a-variable-length-array)Parsing a variable-length array

Parses a variable-length array, requires the length to appear before the array.

This example requires the “parsing_proc” feature (enabled by default)
because it uses the  [ parser_method](https://docs.rs/macro.parser_method.html) macro.

```
use konst::{
    parsing::{Parser, ParseError, parser_method},
    result,
    for_range, try_,
};
// We need to parse the length into a separate const to use it as the length of the array.
const LEN_AND_PARSER: (usize, Parser<'_>) = {
    let input = "\
        6;
        up, 0, 90, down, left, right,
    ";

    let mut parser = Parser::new(input);
    let len = result::unwrap!(parser.parse_usize());
    result::unwrap!(parser.strip_prefix(';'));
    (len, parser)
};
const ANGLES: [Angle; LEN_AND_PARSER.0] =
    result::unwrap!(Angle::parse_array(&mut LEN_AND_PARSER.1));
fn main() {
    assert_eq!(
        ANGLES,
        [Angle::UP, Angle::UP, Angle::RIGHT, Angle::DOWN, Angle::LEFT, Angle::RIGHT]
    );
}
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Copy, Clone)]
struct Angle(u16);
impl Angle {
    pub const UP: Self = Self(0);
    pub const RIGHT: Self = Self(90);
    pub const DOWN: Self = Self(180);
    pub const LEFT: Self = Self(270);
    pub const fn new(n: u64) -> Angle {
        Angle((n % 360) as u16)
    }
    const fn parse_array<'p, const LEN: usize>(
        parser: &mut Parser<'p>
    ) -> Result<[Angle; LEN], ParseError<'p>> {
        let mut ret = [Angle::UP; LEN];

        for_range!{i in 0..LEN =>
            ret[i] = try_!(Angle::parse(parser.trim_start()));

            parser.trim_start();
            if !parser.is_empty() {
                try_!(parser.strip_prefix(','));
            }
        }
        Ok(ret)
    }
    pub const fn parse<'p>(parser: &mut Parser<'p>) -> Result<Angle, ParseError<'p>> {
        if let Ok(angle) = parser.parse_u64() {
            return Ok(Self::new(angle))
        }

        let angle = parser_method!{parser, strip_prefix;
            "up" => Self::UP,
            "right" => Self::RIGHT,
            "down" => Self::DOWN,
            "left" => Self::LEFT,
            _ => return Err(parser.to_other_error(&"could not parse Direction"))
        };
        Ok(angle)
    }
}
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/konst/parsing/non_parsing_methods.rs.html#51-58)#### pub const fn [with_start_offset](https://docs.rs#method.with_start_offset)(string: &'a [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.str.html), start_offset: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.usize.html)) -> Self

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/konst/parsing/non_parsing_methods.rs.html#51-58)

#### pub const fn [with_start_offset](https://docs.rs#method.with_start_offset)(string: &'a [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.str.html), start_offset: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.usize.html)) -> Self

Constructs a Parser from `string` which is at `start_offset`
inside some other string.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use konst::parsing::{ErrorKind, Parser};
// indices
//  0   4   8
//  |   |   |
// "foo bar baz"
let substr = konst::string::str_from("foo bar baz", 4);
let mut parser = Parser::with_start_offset(substr, 4);
assert_eq!(parser.remainder(), "bar baz");
let bar = parser.split(' ').unwrap();
assert_eq!(bar, "bar");
let err = parser.split_terminator(' ').unwrap_err();
assert_eq!(parser.remainder(), "baz");
assert_eq!(err.offset(), 8);
assert_eq!(err.kind(), ErrorKind::DelimiterNotFound);
```
Skips `byte_count` bytes from the parsed string,
as well as however many bytes are required to be on a char boundary.

This method mutates the parser in place.

Skips `byte_count` bytes from the back of the parsed string,
as well as however many bytes are required to be on a char boundary.

This method mutates the parser in place.

#### pub const fn [parse_u128](https://docs.rs#method.parse_u128)(&mut self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[u128](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u128.html), [ParseError](https://docs.rs/struct.ParseError.html)<'a>>

Parses a `u128` until a non-digit is reached.

This method mutates the parser in place on success, leaving it unmodified on error.

To parse an integer from an entire string (erroring on non-digit bytes),
you can use `u128::from_str_radix`

You also can use the [ parse_type](https://docs.rs/macro.parse_type.html)
macro to parse a

`u128`, and other [types.](https://docs.rs/trait.HasParser.html)

`HasParser`[§](https://docs.rs#example-1)Example

```
use konst::{
    parsing::{Parser, ParseError},
    result, try_,
};
{
    let mut parser = Parser::new("12345");
    let num = result::unwrap!(parser.parse_u128());
    assert_eq!(num, 12345);
    assert!(parser.is_empty());
}
/// Parses a `[u128; 2]` from a parser starting with `"<number>;<number>", eg: `"100;400"`.
const fn parse_pair<'a>(parser: &mut Parser<'a>) -> Result<[u128; 2], ParseError<'a>> {
    let mut ret = [0; 2];

    ret[0] = try_!(parser.parse_u128());

    // parsing the `;``between the integers.
    //
    // Note that because we don't use `.trim_start()` afterwards,
    // this can't be followed by spaces.
    try_!(parser.strip_prefix(";"));

    ret[1] = try_!(parser.parse_u128());

    Ok(ret)
}
const PAIR: [u128; 2] = {
    let parser = &mut Parser::new("1365;6789");
    result::unwrap!(parse_pair(parser))
};
assert_eq!(PAIR[0], 1365);
assert_eq!(PAIR[1], 6789);
```

    assert_eq!(result::unwrap!(parser.parse_i128()), -54321);
    assert_eq!(parser.remainder(), ";6789");
    _ = parser.strip_prefix(";");
    assert_eq!(parser.remainder(), "6789");
    assert_eq!(result::unwrap!(parser.parse_i128()), 6789);

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/konst/parsing/primitive_parsing.rs.html#381-395)#### pub const fn [parse_bool](https://docs.rs#method.parse_bool)(&mut self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.bool.html), [ParseError](https://docs.rs/struct.ParseError.html)<'a>>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/konst/parsing/primitive_parsing.rs.html#381-395)

#### pub const fn [parse_bool](https://docs.rs#method.parse_bool)(&mut self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.bool.html), [ParseError](https://docs.rs/struct.ParseError.html)<'a>>

Parses a `bool`.

This method mutates the parser in place on success, leaving it unmodified on error.

To parse a bool from an entire string
(erroring if the string isn’t exactly `"true"` or `"false"`),
you can use `primitive::parse_bool`

You also can use the [ parse_type](https://docs.rs/macro.parse_type.html)
macro to parse a

`bool`, and other [types.](https://docs.rs/trait.HasParser.html)

`HasParser`[§](https://docs.rs#example-12)Example

```
use konst::{Parser, result};
{
    let mut parser = Parser::new("falsemorestring");
    let boolean = result::unwrap!(parser.parse_bool());
    assert_eq!(boolean, false);
    assert_eq!(parser.remainder(), "morestring");
}
{
    let mut parser = Parser::new("truefoo");
    let boolean = result::unwrap!(parser.parse_bool());
    assert_eq!(boolean, true);
    assert_eq!(parser.remainder(), "foo");
}
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/konst/parsing.rs.html#188-210)#### pub const fn [split_terminator](https://docs.rs#method.split_terminator)<'p, P>(
    &mut self,
    delimiter: P,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<&'a [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.str.html), [ParseError](https://docs.rs/struct.ParseError.html)<'a>>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/konst/parsing.rs.html#188-210)

#### pub const fn [split_terminator](https://docs.rs#method.split_terminator)<'p, P>(
    &mut self,
    delimiter: P,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<&'a [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.str.html), [ParseError](https://docs.rs/struct.ParseError.html)<'a>>

Gets the string up to (but not including) `delimiter`.

This method mutates the parser in place on success, leaving it unmodified on error.

This is like [ Parser::split](https://docs.rs/struct.Parser.html#method.split),
except that it always requires that the delimiter can be found.

[§](https://docs.rs#return-value)Return value

If either the string is empty or the delimiter can’t be found, this return an error.

If the delimiter can be found and the string is non-empty. this returns the string before the delimiter, moving the parser to after the delimiter.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-13)Example

```
use konst::{Parser, result};
assert_eq!(VARS, ["foo", "bar", "baz"]);
const VARS: [&str; 3] = {
    let mut parser = Parser::new("foo,bar,baz");

    let foo = result::unwrap!(parser.split_terminator(','));
    let bar = result::unwrap!(parser.split_terminator(','));

    // `.split_terminator(',')` errors here
    // because there's no `,` in the remainder of the string,
    assert!(parser.split_terminator(',').is_err());

    [foo, bar, parser.remainder()]
};
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/konst/parsing.rs.html#311-332)#### pub const fn [split](https://docs.rs#method.split)<'p, P>(
    &mut self,
    delimiter: P,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<&'a [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.str.html), [ParseError](https://docs.rs/struct.ParseError.html)<'a>>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/konst/parsing.rs.html#311-332)

#### pub const fn [split](https://docs.rs#method.split)<'p, P>(
    &mut self,
    delimiter: P,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<&'a [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.str.html), [ParseError](https://docs.rs/struct.ParseError.html)<'a>>

Gets the string up to (but not including) `delimiter`.

[§](https://docs.rs#return-value-2)Return value

If the last delimiter-separated string has already been returned, this return an error.

If the delimiter can’t be found. this returns the remainder of the string.

If the delimiter can be found. this returns the string before the delimiter, moving the parser to after the delimiter.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-15)Example

```
use konst::{Parser, result};
assert_eq!(VARS, ["foo", "bar", ""]);
const VARS: [&str; 3] = {
    let mut parser = Parser::new("foo,bar,");

    let foo = result::unwrap!(parser.split(','));
    let bar = result::unwrap!(parser.split(','));
    let empty = result::unwrap!(parser.split(','));

    assert!(parser.split(',').is_err());
    assert!(parser.remainder().is_empty());

    [foo, bar, empty]
};
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/konst/parsing.rs.html#461-482)#### pub const fn [split_keep](https://docs.rs#method.split_keep)<'p, P>(
    &mut self,
    delimiter: P,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<&'a [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.str.html), [ParseError](https://docs.rs/struct.ParseError.html)<'a>>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/konst/parsing.rs.html#461-482)

#### pub const fn [split_keep](https://docs.rs#method.split_keep)<'p, P>(
    &mut self,
    delimiter: P,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<&'a [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.str.html), [ParseError](https://docs.rs/struct.ParseError.html)<'a>>

Gets the string up to (but not including) `delimiter`.

This method mutates the parser in place on success, leaving it unmodified on error.

[§](https://docs.rs#return-value-4)Return value

This behaves the same as [ Parser::split](https://docs.rs/struct.Parser.html#method.split),
except that it keeps the delimiter in the parser,
rather than skip it.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-17)Example

This example requires the `"parsing_proc"` feature.

```
use konst::{
    parsing::{Parser, ParseError, parser_method},
    result,
    eq_str, for_range, try_,
};
assert_eq!(VALS, [
    Value::Str("hello"),
    Value::U64(3),
    Value::U64(5),
    Value::Str("world"),
]);
const VALS: [Value<'_>; 4] = {
    let mut arr = [Value::Str(""); 4];
    let parser = &mut Parser::new("shello,i3,i5,sworld");

    for_range!{i in 0..arr.len() =>
        arr[i] = result::unwrap!(parse_value(parser));
        if !parser.is_empty() {
            result::unwrap!(parser.strip_prefix(','));
        }
    }

    arr
};
#[derive(Debug, Copy, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Value<'a> {
    Str(&'a str),
    U64(u64),
}
pub const fn parse_value<'p>(parser: &mut Parser<'p>) -> Result<Value<'p>, ParseError<'p>> {
    let val = parser_method!{parser, strip_prefix;
        "s" => {
            let string = try_!(parser.split_keep(','));
            Value::Str(string)
        }
        "i" => {
            let integer = try_!(parser.parse_u64());
            Value::U64(integer)
        }
        _ => return Err(parser.to_other_error(&"expected either `s` or `ì`"))
    };
    Ok(val)
}
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/konst/parsing.rs.html#535-545)#### pub const fn [strip_prefix](https://docs.rs#method.strip_prefix)<'p, P>(
    &mut self,
    matched: P,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<&mut Self, [ParseError](https://docs.rs/struct.ParseError.html)<'a>>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/konst/parsing.rs.html#535-545)

#### pub const fn [strip_prefix](https://docs.rs#method.strip_prefix)<'p, P>(
    &mut self,
    matched: P,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<&mut Self, [ParseError](https://docs.rs/struct.ParseError.html)<'a>>

Checks that the parsed string starts with `matched`,
returning the remainder of the str.

This method mutates the parser in place on success, leaving it unmodified on error.

For calling `strip_prefix` with multiple alternative `matched` string literals,
you can use the [ parser_method](https://docs.rs/macro.parser_method.html) macro,

[example](https://docs.rs/macro.parser_method.html#parsing-enum-example)

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-1)Examples

[§](https://docs.rs#basic)Basic

```
use konst::Parser;
let mut parser = Parser::new("foo;bar;baz;");
assert!(parser.strip_prefix("aaa").is_err());
_ = parser.strip_prefix("foo;");
assert_eq!(parser.remainder(), "bar;baz;");
_ = parser.strip_prefix("bar;");
assert_eq!(parser.remainder(), "baz;");
_ = parser.strip_prefix("baz;");
assert_eq!(parser.remainder(), "");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#char-argument)`char` argument

```
use konst::Parser;
let mut parser = Parser::new("abcde");
_ = parser.strip_prefix('a');
assert_eq!(parser.remainder(), "bcde");
_ = parser.strip_prefix('b');
assert_eq!(parser.remainder(), "cde");
_ = parser.strip_prefix('c');
assert_eq!(parser.remainder(), "de");
```

Removes whitespace from the start of the parsed string.

This method mutates the parser in place.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-19)Example

```
use konst::{Parser, result};
let mut parser = Parser::new("    foo\n\t bar");

Removes whitespace from the end of the parsed string.

This method mutates the parser in place.

```
use konst::{Parser, result};
let mut parser = Parser::new("foo,\n    bar,\n    ");
parser.trim_end();
assert_eq!(parser.remainder(), "foo,\n    bar,");
result::unwrap!(parser.strip_suffix("bar,")).trim_end();
assert_eq!(parser.remainder(), "foo,");
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/konst/parsing.rs.html#771-779)#### pub const fn [trim_start_matches](https://docs.rs#method.trim_start_matches)<'p, P>(&mut self, needle: P) -> &mut Self

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/konst/parsing.rs.html#771-779)

#### pub const fn [trim_start_matches](https://docs.rs#method.trim_start_matches)<'p, P>(&mut self, needle: P) -> &mut Self

Repeatedly removes all instances of `needle` from the start of the parsed string.

This method mutates the parser in place.

For trimming with multiple `needle`s, you can use the [ parser_method](https://docs.rs/macro.parser_method.html) macro,

[example](https://docs.rs/macro.parser_method.html#trimming-example)

[§](https://docs.rs#example-22)Example

[§](https://docs.rs#str-1)`&str`

```
use konst::Parser;
{
    let mut parser = Parser::new("HelloHelloHello world!");
    parser.trim_start_matches("Hello");
    assert_eq!(parser.remainder(), " world!");
}
{
    let mut parser = Parser::new("        Hi!");
    parser.trim_start_matches("    ");
    assert_eq!(parser.remainder(), "Hi!");
}
{
    let mut parser = Parser::new("------Bye!");
    parser.trim_start_matches("----");
    assert_eq!(parser.remainder(), "--Bye!");
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#char-argument-3)`char` argument

```
use konst::Parser;
let mut parser = Parser::new("    ----world");
parser.trim_start_matches(' ');
assert_eq!(parser.remainder(), "----world");
parser.trim_start_matches('-');
assert_eq!(parser.remainder(), "world");
parser.trim_start_matches('-');
assert_eq!(parser.remainder(), "world");
```
